documents.summary: This summer training report details the design and development of an Agentic-AI Based Document Management System created by Rakshit Suneja during his internship at the Bharat Space Education Research Centre. The system utilizes a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline to enable secure document uploads and semantic natural language interaction. Its lightweight agentic architecture features a Coordinator Agent that dynamically routes tasks to dedicated Processing and Search Agents. Implementing JWT-based authentication and Qdrant vector database storage, the project demonstrates advanced skills in full-stack AI development.

 ABSTRACT 
 This  report  presents  the  design  and  development  of  an  Agentic-AI  Based  Document 
 Management  System  ,  undertaken  as  part  of  my  internship,  which  allows  users  to  securely 
 upload  documents  and  interact  with  them  using  natural  language.  Instead  of  manually 
 searching  through  PDFs,  DOCX  files,  and  text  documents,  the  system  automatically  extracts 
 content,  generates  AI-based  summaries  and  metadata,  indexes  documents  using  vector 
 embeddings,  and  enables  users  to  semantically  search  and  "chat"  with  their  documents 
 through a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline[5].

 every  incoming  request  and  routes  it  to  either  a  Processing  Agent  (for  new  document

 2.3 Text Embeddings and Vector Databases 
 Text  embeddings  are  numerical  representations  of  text  that  encode  semantic  and  contextual 
 information  into  high-dimensional  vectors.  Embedding  models  such  as  Sentence 
 Transformers  can  convert  sentences,  paragraphs,  or  document  chunks  into  vector 
 representations,  allowing  semantically  similar  pieces  of  text  to  be  identified  through 
 mathematical similarity measures. 
 The  use  of  embeddings  provides  an  important  advantage  over  conventional  keyword  search. 
 Two  pieces  of  text  can  be  considered  similar  even  when  they  contain  different  words, 
 provided  that  their  underlying  meanings  are  related.  This  makes  embeddings  particularly

 suitable for semantic search and document retrieval applications. 
 As  the  number  of  document  embeddings  increases,  efficient  storage  and  retrieval  become 
 important.  Vector  databases  are  specifically  designed  to  store  high-dimensional  vectors  and 
 perform  similarity  searches  efficiently.  Platforms  such  as  Qdrant,  Pinecone,  and  Weaviate 
 provide specialized indexing and retrieval mechanisms for this purpose.

 are  then  provided  as  contextual  information  to  the  language  model,  which  generates  a 
 response based on the retrieved content.
